title_en: How Much Does A GE9X Engine Cost?
title_zh: GE9X 发动机的成本是多少？
summary: The engine is built exclusively for the Boeing 777X family of aircraft.
summary_zh: 该发动机专为波音 777X 系列飞机制造。
body_en: Luke Diaz is a freelance military writer with experience with active duty experience in the US Navy as well as defense and industrial engineering. He is a former Naval Flight Officer who performed tactical air control on the carrier-based E-2 Hawkeye.

While General Electric has not released an official price list for its enormous GE9X engine , it is estimated to cost between $40 million and $45 million, which adds up to $90 million per Boeing 777-9 on paper. This is significantly more than the retail prices of super-sized widebody powerplants like the GE90 and the Rolls-Royce Trent XWB.

However, commanding the highest commercial engine price in aviation history has not resulted in simple assembly-line profits. Early factory batches cost significantly more to build than launch airline contracts pay back while Boeing finishes testing the airframe. In fact, GE executives warned in January that initial production losses on the GE9X would double this year as shipments increased ahead of commercial service.

Behind that exorbitant price tag lies an unrivaled sole-source agreement on Boeing's flagship twinjet, backed by heat-resistant ceramics, 3D-printed alloys, and record-breaking thrust. However, after volume discounts and multi-year maintenance contracts are factored in, airlines rarely pay anywhere near catalog value. With years of mechanical issues, grounded test aircraft, and mid-turbine seal repairs, this engineering accomplishment has become a high-stakes financial race to 2027.
How A Sole-Source Monopoly & Service Bundles Mask The Real Price

General Electric secured its sole-source grip on the Boeing 777X through a calculated competitive truce years earlier. Back in 2008, GE refused to power the Airbus A350-1000 so it would not undercut its lucrative GE90 franchise on the Boeing 777-300ER. When Boeing later launched the 777X, Pratt & Whitney and Rolls-Royce stayed away after GE Aviation head David Joyce flatly rejected sharing the airframe.

Without a rival engine maker bidding prices down, GE unveiled the GE9X at the 2013 Dubai Air Show alongside massive launch commitments. Emirates agreed to buy 300 engines in a paper deal valued at over $11 billion, roughly $37 million apiece before discounts, while Qatar Airways followed with a $3.8 billion order covering 50 jets. However, if carriers negotiate significant volume discounts, actual airline invoices hardly resemble flashy airshow figures.

GE frequently incorporates engine hardware into multi-year service contracts in order to further obfuscate per-unit pricing. For instance, because it included a 12-year TrueChoice overhaul agreement, Singapore Airlines' 2022 order for 22 spare GE9X engines had a $2.8 billion headline value, well over $100 million per engine. With this 'razor-and-blades' strategy, GE is able to absorb early production losses while securing three decades of revenue from sole-source repairs on demanding ultra-long-haul routes.
Why GE Detuned A World-Record Engine To Save Fuel

Raw mechanical muscle anchors the GE9X's lofty sticker price, proven during a November 2017 ground run in Peebles, Ohio, when a test engine hit 134,300 pounds of thrust (597 kN) to claim a Guinness World Record. After the historic test , Joyce said: "While we didn't set out to break the thrust Guinness World Records title, we are proud of the engine's performance, which is a testament to our talented employees and partners who design and build outstanding products for our customers."

Airline pilots will never use that record power on a routine departure. That's because General Electric purposefully derated the production turbofan below the 115,300 pounds of thrust (513 kN) of its earlier GE90-115B brother. With the help of a front fan bigger than a Boeing 737-800 cabin and 16 steel-tipped carbon-fiber blades that reduce fuel consumption by 10%, the operating cooler prolongs the time between shop overhauls, maintains costly core blades, and saves fuel over thousands of flights.

Size and efficiency anchored GE's sales pitch to global long-haul carriers when US regulators cleared the engine in September 2020. According to Composites World, GE Aviation CEO John Slattery declared at certification: "There is no substitute that can achieve the combination of size, power and fuel efficiency." Test flights aboard GE's Boeing 747-400 flying testbed even ran so quietly that a pilot checked cockpit gauges just to confirm the engine was still running.
Space-Age Ceramics And 300 3D-Printed Parts Drive Up The Bill

The engine's core is made of exotic, heat-resistant materials, which contribute significantly to its price tag of over $40 million. Ceramic matrix composites, lightweight, space-age ceramics that can resist temperatures up to 2,400°F (1,315°C) without melting, are packed into the GE9X's combustor and turbine. This allows the engine to run hotter and more effectively while requiring far less cooling air. Program leader Ted Ingling stated: "The ceramics allowed us to go to 60:1 [pressure ratio] inside the GE9X. So if I'm Boeing and I'm looking for the lightest-weight engine so that I can turn that weight into passengers - it's range, it's fuel, it's passengers."

Industrial 3D printing increases costs by generating over 300 complicated pieces per engine, such as one-piece fuel nozzles that reduce weight by 25% and electron-beam-melted titanium-aluminum turbine blades. Even with unusual alloys, engineers strove to make layouts tidy enough for line mechanics. In November 2025, GE Aerospace technology chief Mohamed Ali stated: "There is elegance in simplicity with the fewest number of parts. If the architecture is done correctly, you'll occasionally have to fix a sink or replace appliances, but the house functions and is practical."
Billions In Losses Force Airlines To Keep Aging Quadjets Flying

The GE9X has had a difficult development process, characterized by frequent technical setbacks that have repeatedly delayed Boeing's certification deadline, despite its exorbitant valuation. The 777-9's first flight was postponed until engineers completed a permanent redesign in 2019 due to early compressor vane wear, which required General Electric to airlift four engines back to its facilities by Antonov freighters.

Long after the engine was certified by US regulators in September 2020, new mechanical curveballs caused turbulence during flight testing. All four 777-9 prototypes were grounded for five months after a titanium thrust link broke on a test plane returning from Hawaii in late 2022. In January 2026, shop inspectors found a damaged mid-turbine seal that was prematurely wearing due to excessive heat stress.
body_zh: 卢克·迪亚兹 (Luke Diaz) 是一位自由军事作家，拥有在美国海军以及国防和工业工程领域服役的现役经验。他是一名前海军飞行军官，曾在舰载 E-2 鹰眼上执行战术空中控制。
虽然通用电气尚未公布其巨型 GE9X 发动机的官方价格表，但估计其成本在 4000 万至 4500 万美元之间，每架波音 777-9 的纸面价格总计为 9000 万美元。这明显高于 GE90 和劳斯莱斯遄达 XWB 等超大型宽体发动机的零售价。
然而，掌握航空史上最高的商用发动机价格并没有带来简单的装配线利润。早期工厂批次的建造成本远高于波音公司完成机身测试后启动航空公司合同的成本。事实上，GE 高管在一月份警告称，随着商业服务之前出货量的增加，GE9X 今年的初始生产损失将翻倍。
高昂价格的背后是波音旗舰双发喷气式飞机无与伦比的独家来源协议，该协议以耐热陶瓷、3D 打印合金和破纪录的推力为后盾。然而，在考虑到批量折扣和多年维护合同后，航空公司很少支付接近目录价格的费用。经过多年的机械问题、停飞的测试飞机和涡轮机中部密封修复，这项工程成就已成为 2027 年的一场高风险的财务竞赛。
单一来源垄断和服务捆绑如何掩盖真实价格

通用电气通过几年前精心策划的竞争休战，确保了对波音 777X 的唯一供应商控制。早在 2008 年，GE 就拒绝为空客 A350-1000 提供动力，以免削弱其利润丰厚的 GE90 在波音 777-300ER 上的特许经营权。当波音后来推出 777X 时，通用电气航空集团 (GE Aviation) 负责人戴维·乔伊斯 (David Joyce) 断然拒绝共享机身，普惠公司 (Pratt & Whitney) 和劳斯莱斯 (Rolls-Royce) 都没有参与。
由于没有竞争对手的发动机制造商压低价格，GE 在 2013 年迪拜航展上推出了 GE9X，并做出了大规模的发布承诺。阿联酋航空同意在一份价值超过 110 亿美元的纸面交易中购买 300 台发动机，折价前每台发动机约为 3,700 万美元，卡塔尔航空紧随其后，签订了价值 38 亿美元的订单，涵盖 50 架飞机。然而，如果航空公司协商大幅折扣，实际的航空公司发票就很难与华丽的航展数字相媲美。
通用电气经常将发动机硬件纳入多年服务合同中，以进一步混淆单位定价。例如，由于新加坡航空 2022 年订购的 22 架备用 GE9X 发动机包含一项为期 12 年的 TrueChoice 大修协议，其总价值为 28 亿美元，每台发动机远远超过 1 亿美元。通过这种“剃刀和刀片”战略，GE 能够吸收早期的生产损失，同时从要求苛刻的超长途航线的独家维修中获得三十年的收入。
为什么通用电气为了节省燃油而对世界纪录的发动机进行失谐
原始的机械肌肉支撑着 GE9X 的高昂标价，这一点在 2017 年 11 月俄亥俄州皮布尔斯的地面运行中得到了证明，当时测试发动机达到了 134,300 磅的推力（597 kN），创造了吉尼斯世界纪录。在这次历史性的测试之后，乔伊斯表示：“虽然我们并没有打算打破推力吉尼斯世界纪录称号，但我们对发动机的性能感到自豪，这证明了我们才华横溢的员工和合作伙伴为我们的客户设计和制造了出色的产品。”
航空公司飞行员永远不会在例行起飞时使用这种创纪录的功率。这是因为通用电气故意将量产型涡轮风扇发动机的推力降低到低于其早期 GE90-115B 兄弟产品的 115,300 磅推力（513 kN）。借助比波音 737-800 客舱还大的前风扇和 16 个钢头碳纤维叶片，可降低 10% 的燃油消耗，运行冷却器延长了车间大修之间的时间，维护了昂贵的核心叶片，并在数千次飞行中节省了燃油。
当美国监管机构于 2020 年 9 月批准该发动机时，尺寸和效率成为了 GE 对全球长途航空公司的销售宣传。据 Composites World 报道，GE 航空首席执行官 John Slattery 在认证时宣称：“没有任何替代品可以实现尺寸、功率和燃油效率的结合。” GE 的波音 747-400 飞行试验台上的试飞甚至运行得非常安静，以至于飞行员检查驾驶舱仪表只是为了确认发动机仍在运行。
太空时代陶瓷和 300 个 3D 打印零件推高了价格

该发动机的核心由特殊的耐热材料制成，这使其售价超过 4000 万美元。 GE9X 的燃烧室和涡轮机采用陶瓷基复合材料，这是一种轻质太空时代陶瓷，可承受高达 2,400°F (1,315°C) 的温度而不熔化。这使得发动机能够更热、更有效地运行，同时需要更少的冷却空气。项目负责人 Ted Ingling 表示：“陶瓷使我们能够在 GE9X 内部达到 60:1 [压力比]。因此，如果我是波音公司，我正在寻找重量最轻的发动机，这样我就可以将重量转化为乘客 - 它是航程、它是燃料、它是乘客。”

工业 3D 打印每台发动机需要生成 300 多个复杂部件，例如重量减轻 25% 的一体式燃油喷嘴和电子束熔化钛铝涡轮叶片，从而增加了成本。即使使用不寻常的合金，工程师们也努力使布局对于生产线机械来说足够整洁。 2025 年 11 月，GE 航空航天技术负责人穆罕默德·阿里 (Mohamed Ali) 表示：“用最少的部件打造简约中的优雅。如果建筑设计正确，你偶尔需要修理水槽或更换电器，但房子功能齐全且实用。”
数十亿美元的损失迫使航空公司继续使用老化的四轴喷气式飞机
GE9X的开发过程很艰难，其特点是频繁的技术挫折，导致波音公司的认证期限一再推迟，尽管其估值过高。由于压缩机叶片早期磨损，777-9 的首飞被推迟，直到工程师在 2019 年完成永久性重新设计，这需要通用电气通过安东诺夫货机将四台发动机空运回其设施。
该发动机于 2020 年 9 月获得美国监管机构认证很久之后，新的机械曲线球在飞行测试期间引起了湍流。 2022 年底从夏威夷返回的一架测试飞机上，钛合金推力连杆断裂后，所有四架 777-9 原型机都停飞了五个月。2026 年 1 月，车间检查员发现涡轮中部密封件损坏，由于热应力过大而过早磨损。

title_en: The Forgotten Pacific Airfield Where WWII Fighter Planes Are Being Reclaimed By The Jungle
title_zh: 被遗忘的太平洋机场，二战战斗机正在被丛林收复
summary: The island of Yap is full of lost Japanese WWII aircraft wrecks, with some US aircraft like Corsairs also to be found.
summary_zh: 雅浦岛到处都是二战时期日本失落的飞机残骸，还发现了一些美国飞机，如海盗船。
body_en: Aaron is an aviation enthusiast and world traveler with a deep interest in aerospace history and technology. He has traveled around the world numerous times, often incorporating visits to aviation museums and historic aircraft collections into his journeys. A native of New Zealand, he is an expert in aviation and maintains a broad interest in a variety of other subjects.

It is well known that many World War II fighter wrecks lie across the islands of the Pacific. Many of these are lost, forgotten, or abandoned, left to rot in jungles. Others lie in shallow waters, becoming refuges for marine life and attractions for today's divers. In October and November, I visited the island nations of Palau and the Federated States of Micronesia FSM (Yap Island), where the remains of WWII are everywhere. Only a very limited number of rather niche divers seem to be the only true tourists Yap attracts today.

While various Japanese bunkers, radio buildings, light-rail trains, and guns are found across Palau, most of the fighting is on the smaller island of Peleliu. Unfortunately, I didn't visit Peleliu, although I did visit Yap. Peleliu was the site of one of the deadliest Marine operations. Conversely, invasion plans for Yap were scrapped, and the island was bombarded and bypassed. Today, visitors can see Japanese WWII aircraft lying, reclaimed by the jungle where they were destroyed .

The island of Yap was controlled by Spain until the Spanish-American War of 1898, when it lost Cuba, Puerto Rico, the Philippines, and Guam to the United States. Spain was left with a large expanse of small Micronesian islands that the United States did not take over but could not defend. It promptly sold the islands to the emerging German Empire.

As World War I broke out, Japan quickly seized most of the German Pacific islands, although Australia took Nauru and New Guinea and New Zealand took German Samoa. The former German islands were then run by Japan under the League of Nations South Seas Mandate. It appears from Japanese colonization of the islands that Japan planned to integrate these islands, including Yap, into Japan proper, although this never happened.

When the Pacific War broke out, Japan had managed Yap for around 35 years and was busy populating the island. During the war, it fortified the islands to create a defensive ring to defend the Japanese home islands. The US Navy launched its famous island-hopping campaign to bring its bombers within range of the home islands. For a brief period of time in 1944, Yap found itself at the center of the Pacific War.

The Japanese military buildup on Yap began relatively late, and it was not heavily fortified before the Pacific War. The island lacked a good natural harbor and had few natural defensive strong points. The most significant Japanese installation was the airfield at Lamer, located adjacent to the modern Yap International Airport.

The runway was built using reef material, although locals told me that the Japanese also used thousands of their famous money stones (Rai). By April 1944, the main strip was completed while some of the supporting infrastructure was unfinished. The site's main purpose was to establish an air transit and staging point for Japanese aircraft moving across the region. The combined Japanese Army and Navy garrison on the island totaled around 4,000 to 5,000 men.

The US had intended to invade the island, but instead opted for bombing, neutralizing, and bypassing it. By May and June, Japan was deploying aircraft to the island. American reconnaissance reported 24 Japanese fighters, six dive bombers, two medium bombers, and six night fighters. The aircraft soon became a target for American long-range B-24 bombers . By September, Americans were encountering little or no aerial resistance from the island.

After the war, the bombed-out Japanese airfield appears to have been abandoned. The forests regrew and reclaimed the airfield, while locals treated the runway as a roadway and built their homes along it. Today, some Japanese wrecks are located next to homes. Visitors can go and explore the old airbase and find the wrecks, as I did. There are World War II marker signs at most of the notable wrecks, but some are not marked. The signs are often not maintained and can be lost over time.

Almost all the land on Yap is privately owned, and visitors are expected to ask landowners for permission before seeing the wrecks, even if they are marked and signed. In all, I found the wrecks of around eight Japanese aircraft, including a Mitsubishi G4M 'Betty' bomber. Bizarrely, the Betty bomber now lies next to a Boeing 727 that crashed next to it decades later.

The runway is in poor shape, and it is extensively potholed and overgrown. It is lined with abandoned cars rotting in the jungle. Yap may be famous for its stone money, but having explored the island, it is hard not to also associate it with endless abandoned, decaying cars. Aircraft wrecks can generally be found between 150 and 300 feet (45 to 91 meters) from the runway.

The Mitsubishi G4M bomber is one of the most notable wrecks . It was a medium bomber/torpedo bomber, with Japan building 2,435 examples of the type. It had a crew of seven. Another notable wreck is a Japanese Nakajima B5N Torpedo Bomber. These were three-man carrier-based torpedo bombers, of which Japan built 1,149 units. A number of Mitsubishi A6M Zero fighters can also be found.

I found two small tails of wrecked aircraft that I assumed were Zeros, but they were unmarked, and I couldn't tell for sure. The Google Maps screenshot above marks the locations on the old airfield where I found Japanese wrecks. There are likely many more to be found, but this is private land, and the jungle is extremely thick, making movement and visibility very difficult.
Japanese aircraft on Yap (per 1944 US reconnaissance )

All around the airfield, large bomb craters from US bomb strikes are visible. I am used to finding these bomb craters in Vietnam. Many are visible at Vietnam's historic site of My Son, but they always seem to be difficult to make out in photos, especially when they are surrounded by thick jungles. One of the aircraft wrecks I found was next to a bomb crater, and I had to climb in and out of the crater to get around what was left of the aircraft.

Across the island, I saw many other remains of WWII. These include a well-marked Japanese Type 88 75mm anti-air gun preserved next to some Zero fighters . On the main hill overlooking the main settlement of Colonia, I found four more Japanese guns with the barrels destroyed. These were marked, but they are overgrown, and the signs have largely disappeared.
body_zh: 亚伦是一位航空爱好者和环球旅行家，对航空航天历史和技术有着浓厚的兴趣。他曾多次环游世界，经常在旅途中参观航空博物馆和历史飞机收藏。他是新西兰人，是航空专家，并对其他各种学科保持着广泛的兴趣。
众所周知，太平洋岛屿上散布着许多二战战斗机残骸。其中许多都丢失、被遗忘或被遗弃，在丛林中腐烂。其他的则位于浅水中，成为海洋生物的避难所和当今潜水员的景点。 10月和11月，我访问了帕劳岛国和密克罗尼西亚联邦（雅浦岛），那里到处都是二战遗迹。如今，雅浦岛吸引的唯一真正的游客似乎只有数量非常有限的小众潜水员。
虽然帕劳各地都有各种日本掩体、无线电大楼、轻轨列车和枪支，但大部分战斗发生在较小的贝里琉岛。不幸的是，虽然我访问了雅浦岛，但我没有访问贝里琉岛。贝里琉岛是海军陆战队伤亡最惨重的行动之一。相反，雅浦岛的入侵计划被取消，该岛遭到轰炸并被绕过。今天，游客可以看到日本二战飞机躺在被摧毁的丛林中。
雅浦岛一直由西班牙控制，直到 1898 年美西战争，当时雅浦岛将古巴、波多黎各、菲律宾和关岛拱手让给了美国。西班牙留下了大片密克罗尼西亚小岛，美国没有接管但也无法保卫这些岛屿。它立即将这些岛屿卖给了新兴的德意志帝国。
第一次世界大战爆发后，日本迅速占领了大部分德属太平洋岛屿，澳大利亚占领了瑙鲁和新几内亚，新西兰占领了德属萨摩亚。这些前德国岛屿随后由日本根据国际联盟南海托管管辖权管理。从日本对这些岛屿的殖民统治来看，日本计划将包括雅浦岛在内的这些岛屿纳入日本本土，尽管这从未发生过。
太平洋战争爆发时，日本管理雅浦岛约 35 年，并忙于在岛上繁衍人口。战争期间，它在岛屿上筑垒，形成防御圈，保卫日本本土。美国海军发起了著名的跳岛行动，将轰炸机带到本岛的射程内。 1944 年的一段短暂时间内，雅浦发现自己处于太平洋战争的中心。
日本在雅浦岛的军事集结起步较晚，在太平洋战争之前也没有重兵防守。该岛缺乏良好的天然良港，自然防御据点也很少。日本最重要的设施是位于现代雅浦国际机场附近的拉默机场。
跑道是用珊瑚礁材料建造的，尽管当地人告诉我，日本人也使用了数千颗他们著名的金钱石（Rai）。到 1944 年 4 月，主要地带已竣工，但一些配套基础设施尚未完工。该站点的主要目的是为穿越该地区的日本飞机建立一个空中过境和中转站。日本陆军和海军在岛上的驻军总数约为 4,000 至 5,000 人。
美国原本打算入侵该岛，但最终选择了轰炸、压制和绕行。到五月和六月，日本已向该岛部署飞机。美国侦察报告称，有 24 架日本战斗机、六架俯冲轰炸机、两架中型轰炸机和六架夜间战斗机。该机很快成为美国远程 B-24 轰炸机的目标。到九月，美国人几乎没有遇到来自该岛的空中抵抗。
战后，被炸毁的日本机场似乎已被废弃。森林重新生长并开垦了机场，而当地人则将跑道视为道路并沿其建造了房屋。如今，一些日本沉船残骸位于房屋旁边。游客可以像我一样去探索旧空军基地并寻找残骸。大多数著名沉船残骸上都有二战标记，但也有一些没有标记。这些标志通常得不到维护，并且随着时间的推移可能会丢失。
雅浦岛几乎所有土地都是私人拥有的，游客在观看沉船之前应该征求土地所有者的许可，即使它们有标记和签名。我总共发现了大约八架日本飞机的残骸，其中包括一架三菱 G4M“贝蒂”轰炸机。奇怪的是，贝蒂轰炸机现在躺在一架几十年后坠毁的波音 727 飞机旁边。
跑道状况不佳，坑坑洼洼，杂草丛生。它两旁都是在丛林中腐烂的废弃汽车。雅浦岛可能因其石钱而闻名，但探索过这个岛后，很难不把它与无尽的废弃、腐烂的汽车联系起来。飞机残骸通常可以在距跑道 150 至 300 英尺（45 至 91 米）的地方发现。
三菱 G4M 轰炸机是最著名的残骸之一。这是一款中型轰炸机/鱼雷轰炸机，日本建造了 2,435 架该类型飞机。它有七名船员。另一件值得注意的残骸是日本中岛 B5N 鱼雷轰炸机。这些是三人舰载鱼雷轰炸机，日本建造了 1,149 架。还可以找到一些三菱 A6M 零式战斗机。
我发现了两架失事飞机的小尾翼，我认为它们是零式飞机，但它们没有标记，我无法确定。上面的谷歌地图屏幕截图标记了我在旧机场发现日本残骸的位置。可能还会发现更多，但这是私人土地，丛林极其茂密，移动和能见度都非常困难。
雅浦岛的日本飞机（根据 1944 年美国侦察）
机场周围随处可见美国轰炸造成的巨大弹坑。我习惯在越南寻找这些弹坑。在越南的美山古迹中可以看到许多这样的生物，但它们似乎总是很难在照片中辨认出来，尤其是当它们被茂密的丛林包围时。我发现的一架飞机残骸靠近一个炸弹坑，我必须在弹坑里爬进爬出才能绕过飞机的残骸。
在岛上，我看到了许多其他二战遗迹。其中包括一门标记清晰的日本 88 型 75 毫米高射炮，保存在一些零式战斗机旁边。在俯瞰科洛尼亚主要定居点的主山上，我发现了另外四门日本枪，枪管已被摧毁。这些都有标记，但它们杂草丛生，而且标记基本上已经消失了。

body_en: Selected U.S. Military Contracts for the Week of March 6 - March 10, 2017 user+1@localho… Wed, 03/15/2017 - 01:41 Selected U.S. military contracts for March 6, 2017 U.S. ARMY Blue Storm Associates Inc. , doing business as Pemdas Technologies and Innovation, Alexandria, Virginia, was awarded a $49,500,000 order dependent contract for the Atmospheric Sensing and Prediction System. Bids were solicited via the internet with one received. U.S. Army Contracting Command, Research Triangle Park, North Carolina, is the contracting activity (W911NF-17-D-0001). Selected U.S. military contracts for March 7, 2017 U.S. AIR FORCE Kelly Aviation Center LP , San Antonio, has been awarded a $1,001,978,024 indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for KC-10 engine contractor logistic support. Contractor will provide engine teardown and overhaul, on-wing support/contract field teams, and engine parts and logistics. In addition, the contractor will provide all support required to fulfill this requirement, including but not limited to labor, materials, tools, equipment, parts, and transportation. Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, Tinker AFB, Oklahoma, is the contracting activity (FA8105-17-D-0002). U.S. NAVY Avian LLC , Lexington Park, Maryland, is being awarded an $11,402,443 cost-plus-fixed-fee contract to provide support for the Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division’s Integrated System Evaluation Experimentation and Test Department (AIR-5.1). Services provided will include flight test engineering, programmatic, administrative, design, execution, analysis, evaluation, and reporting of tests and experiments of aircraft, unmanned air systems, weapons and weapons systems. The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division, Patuxent River, Maryland, is the contracting activity (N00421-17-C-0049). Selected U.S. military contracts for March 8, 2017 U.S. NAVY Sierra Nevada Corp. , Rancho, California, is being awarded a $30,995,905 modification to a previously awarded firm-fixed-price, cost-plus-fixed-fee, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract (N00174-09-D-0003) to extend the ordering period and exercise Option Year 6 for the procurement and support of the transmitting set, countermeasures AN/PLT-5, to support explosive ordnance disposal personnel. The AN/PLT-5 is a man-portable system in support of the Joint Service Explosive Ordnance Disposal Counter Radio Controlled Improvised Explosive Device Electronic Warfare program. The Naval Surface Warfare Center Indian Head Explosive Ordnance Disposal Technology Division, Indian Head, Maryland, is the contracting activity. Vector Planning and Services Inc. , San Diego, is being awarded a potential $17,910,070 indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity, cost-plus-fixed-fee contract to provide cyberspace science, research, engineering, and technology integration. Support includes innovative technology assessment and development; rapid software development and prototyping; enabling capability training; security engineering; and cybersecurity risk management. This is one of four multiple-award contracts. All awardees will have the opportunity to compete for task orders during the ordering period. The Space and Naval Warfare Systems Center Pacific, San Diego, is the contracting activity (N66001-17-D-0117). Selected U.S. military contracts for March 9, 2017 U.S. MISSILE DEFENSE AGENCY Lockheed Martin Space Systems Co. , Sunnyvale, California, was awarded a $53,052,807 competitive cost-plus-fixed-fee contract for a 36-month period with no options for the Multi-Object Kill Vehicle Technology Risk Reduction (TRR) effort. This contract represents part of the Missile Defense Agency’s technology risk reduction strategy to improve performance and reduce risk for a gimbaled seeker assembly, integrated avionics assembly, component integration and testing, and an advanced seeker. The Missile Defense Agency, Huntsville, Alabama, is the contracting activity (HQ0147-17-C-0002). U.S. NAVY ViON Corp. , Herndon, California, is being awarded a $34,790,000 indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract to provide Capacity as a Service support to Space and Naval Warfare Systems Command (Spawar) Headquarters, Spawar System Center Pacific and Spawar System Center Atlantic. The Capacity as a Service acquisition model allows Spawar to more accurately scale, up and down, its information technology (IT) infrastructure to meet evolving mission requirements. Savings are realized through no up-front costs and a “pay as you go” acquisition model, reducing waste usually associated with overbuying of IT equipment to eventually meet an expectation of mission requirement. Under this contract, ViON is responsible for providing on-demand, on-premise computing, networking and storage solutions for a variety of systems and applications for the command’s research, development, testing and evaluation core infrastructures, laboratory and data center environments. This contract includes options, which if exercised, would bring the maximum contract value to $49,990,000. The Space and Naval Warfare Systems Command, San Diego, is the contracting activity (N00039-17-D-0003). Aerospace and Defense companies such as yours are looking for ways to gain insight into program decisions that impact cost, timing and quality. To effectively compete and achieve program execution excellence, you need to make manufacturing a core part of the development process. Put your Product Realization knowledge to test with this pop quiz. Complete the short quiz and be entered to win one of two $50 Amazon gifts cards! Test Your Product Realization Knowledge What is product realization for Aerospace and Defense companies? It is the final phase of the project It is a process-driven approach to the entire manufacturing lifecycle starting with “Concept to build” through “Build to delivery” It is the decision that a design meets all requirements of OEMs and suppliers How does a product realization solution support program execution excellence? Through simulation of production alternatives to virtually verify the manufacturing processes and tooling throughout the entire manufacturing lifecycle – full digital twin Through concurrent maturing of manufacturing processes and tooling with the design thus impacting the design prior to release Through integration of advanced manufacturing technologies and automation with the ability to virtually commission robotics and CNC equipment Through the ability to trace a requirement to a design feature to an inspection within the electronic work instructions – complete digital thread Through the ability to easily and electronically compare the as-designed to as-built for delivery – complete digital thread All of the above Name the product realization strategy that helps understand the manufacturing implications of multiple design alternatives. body_en: Autoflight V5000 Matrix william.moore@… Tue, 03/31/2026 - 07:48 The V5000 Matrix is a lift-plus-cruise hybrid-electric/all-electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft being developed by AutoFlight Europe GmbH. Unveiled in February 2026, the aircraft performed a remotely piloted transition from thrustborne hover to wingborne cruise, demonstrating that flight testing is already underway. Industry commentators have suggested that entry into service could be as soon as 2027/2028, although there is no confirmation of this. Certification is to be sought from the Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC) under powered-lift regulations. Structure and Powertrain The Matrix pushes regulations to their maximum, being a 10 seat eVTOL with a maximum take-off weight of 5,700kg (hybrid version). The aircraft could be configured in a 6-seat VIP layout, or a 9-seat business layout plus a pilot. It will also feature a lavatory, the first eVTOL design to incorporate this, an indication of its lengthier flight duration capabilities. An uncrewed cargo variant is also in development. The intended market is more regional-focused than previous eVTOL designs. Structurally, the V5000 is an evolution of the previous Autoflight Prosperity I and CarryAll cargo variant. It features a long, aerodynamic cabin with panoramic viewing windows and skid-style landing gear. A main high wing is complemented by two smaller wings to the front and rear of the aircraft, with three booms extending across all three wings parallel to the cabin, on each side. 20 two-blade fixed propellers are mounted to the six booms to provide lift, while eight cruise propellers provide forward thrust, four mounted to the front and four to the rear. summary: Turkey Signs $11 Billion Eurofighter Deal hockensmithawi… Mon, 10/27/2025 - 18:19 Turkey has signed a long-anticipated £8 billion ($11 billion) deal to acquire Eurofighter Typhoons, the first major export contract for the four-nation combat aircraft since 2017

body_en: Turkey Signs $11 Billion Eurofighter Deal hockensmithawi… Mon, 10/27/2025 - 18:19 Turkey has signed a long-anticipated £8 billion ($11 billion) deal to acquire Eurofighter Typhoons, the first major export contract for the four-nation combat aircraft since 2017. Twenty new-built aircraft will be purchased in the country’s first acquisition of a European combat aircraft after decades of operating new and secondhand U.S.-built fighters. But Turkey’s Eurofighter order could more than double in size, according to Turkish Defense Minister Yasar Guler. He declared that Ankara would also buy another 24 aircraft second hand, 12 each from Oman and Qatar. If those sales go through, Oman would be giving up Eurofighter operations. With deliveries of the new-build aircraft not due until 2030, delivering those second-hand aircraft—potentially as early as next year from Qatar, according to Guler—would allow Turkey to accelerate the Eurofighter’s entry into service and enable the retirement of older aircraft from its inventory, including the McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom. BAE Systems, which will produce the newly built aircraft in Warton, England, says it will receive £5.4 billion of the £8 billion deal. Included in the £5.4 billion are the aircraft and the weapons package from MBDA, including some integration work, potentially for Turkish indigenous weaponry. The remaining £2.6 billion is support and training activity, which will be contracted later, BAE Systems officials say. It is unclear whether the deal will ultimately include offsets to enable Turkish industry to become involved in the Eurofighter program and for Turkey to have a level of freedom of action for the fleet. After decades of facing numerous arms embargoes, Turkey often demands the ability to locally perform airframe, system and engine maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) in-country. The deal was struck during a meeting between UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan in Ankara. Starmer said the deal was a win for British workers and the wider UK defense industry. Government officials claim the order is “saving the Warton production line,” after concerns about a lack of new orders for UK-built Typhoons were expressed by workers unions. UK industry has a 37% share in the Eurofighter program and production of major component assemblies is being ramped up thanks to orders from the other Eurofighter partner nations including Germany, Italy and Spain. “Today’s announcement extends Typhoon production and preserves crucial sovereign skills which underpin the UK’s defense and security,” BAE Systems CEO Charles Woodburn said. The deal is another major boost for the UK defense industry, coming just weeks after the UK’s Type 26 frigates were selected by Norway in a £10 billion deal. UK Defense Secretary John Healey said the deal went beyond the procurement of aircraft. “It is the leading edge of the growing defense and industrial partnership between our two nations,” he said. As part of the visit, Starmer also visited the facilities of Turkish Aerospace Industries, where he was shown the indigenous Kaan combat aircraft. He was also exposed to the Hurjet advanced jet trainer, a potential candidate to replace the BAE Systems Hawk jet trainer in the UK Royal Air Force (RAF) inventory. The deal follows three years of negotiations, which have included lobbying of the German government for Berlin to lift a restriction on a Eurofighter sale after Erdoğan’s government arrested Istanbul Mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu, who is seen as a serious presidential rival to Erdoğan in upcoming elections. The administration of German Chancellor Friedrich Merz lifted the sanctions in part because of the benefit to German industry. A memorandum of understanding between the UK and Turkish governments for a Eurofighter sale was agreed to in July. Turkey’s interest in the aircraft is driven in part by a need for a more capable air combat platform to be available in the interim until advanced versions of the Kaan aircraft are produced in the 2030s. Ankara’s decision to opt for a European fighter, meanwhile, will have been driven by a need to diversify sources of supply after facing sanctions from the U.S. over its purchase of a Russian air defense system and banishment from the F-35 Joint Strike Fighter program. The transfer of Omani and Qatari aircraft to Turkey begs questions over the future of additional Eurofighter orders from Qatar, which has long been linked to orders for a further 12 aircraft for a total of 36. Oman, meanwhile, appears to want to consolidate its fighter fleet around the Lockheed Martin F-16 Block 50. In BAE Systems’ 2023 full-year results, the company revealed that the Omani air force had chosen not to renew support arrangements for its Typhoons, and it is unclear how active that fleet now is. Buying these additional aircraft would mean Turkey would have a mix of three configurations in its fleet. Qatar’s aircraft have the Mk.0 version of the active electronically scanned array European Common Radar System (ECRS) radar, while Oman’s feature the mechanically scanned Captor sensor. In addition to the Eurofighter order, Erdoğan and Starmer also revealed they were working on a new trade and security pact. body_en: Project Lotus, Northrop Grumman’s Secret Autonomous Aircraft Revealed hockensmithawi… Mon, 10/27/2025 - 18:05 Northrop Grumman has secretly built a large new uncrewed aircraft system (UAS), dubbed Project Lotus, at the company’s Scaled Composites rapid prototyping facility in Mojave, California, a source familiar with the project tells Aviation Week. A photo of the aircraft reviewed by Aviation Week revealed a completed, turbofan-powered aircraft parked within the Scaled Composites compound at the public airport. The Lotus UAS design in some ways resembles features of the newly revealed Lockheed Martin Project Vectis, with a long, slender fuselage positioned forward of the leading edges of the wings, capped by a nose with swept-back edges leading to a slender point. In many other respects, the Lotus and Vectis designs diverge. Unlike the engine inlet mounted low at mid-fuselage for the Vectis aircraft, the Lotus inlet sits high atop of the extreme aft section of its fuselage. The Lotus also sports sharply canted tails, breaking from the tailless-configured Vectis. Project Lotus appears to represent Northrop’s candidate for the U.S. Air Force’s Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) Increment 2 program, which is finalizing requirements for competitive prototypes ahead of a scheduled acquisition process next year. The photo reveals that Northrop has already built a demonstrator, perhaps gaining a step on Lockheed’s rival design, which is not scheduled to reach first flight until 2027. As Northrop’s rapid prototyping arm, the Scaled Composites facility frequently builds aircraft demonstrators in secret. Scaled Composites registered a turbofan-powered, fixed-wing aircraft identified only as Model 444 earlier this year with the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), which granted the organization the N444LX tail number. It is not clear if the registration represents Project Lotus or another undisclosed project. Northrop also is building the XRQ-73, also known as the Series Hybrid Electric Propulsion AiR Demonstration (Shepard), for DARPA. In response to questions about Project Lotus from Aviation Week, Northrop avoided direct answers, but spoke generally about its internal investments in autonomous aircraft. “Our investments prioritize production at speed and scale, without sacrificing performance or capability. The Northrop Grumman team has generated step-change advancements in production speed, weight and parts reduction, and overall cost efficiency. These advancements benefit the spectrum of autonomous capabilities we produce at Northrop Grumman for U.S. and international customers,” Northrop said. As Lockheed’s Project Vectis design revealed in September, Northrop’s Project Lotus represents one side in a long-running debate within industry and the Air Force over the future direction of the CCA fleet between concepts that emphasize greater survivability or lower cost. In 2024, the Air Force decided to seek a middle ground between cost and survivability with the selected competitive prototypes for the CCA Increment 1 program. The General Atomics Aeronautical Systems Inc. YFQ-42 and Anduril YFQ-44 are large aircraft that feature some low-observable, or stealth, technology. But the aircraft are larger and costlier than, for example, the Kratos XQ-58, and lack the stealthier features of Project Vectis and Project Lotus. In September, Air Force officials said they were considering the full spectrum of options for the Increment 2 CCA requirement, ranging from exquisite survivability to small, air-launched systems. Project Lotus also lends new insight into how Northrop’s internal CCA concepts have evolved from previous, publicly released ideas. As the Air Force competition for CCAs heated up in 2023, Northrop showed off the SG-1 and SG-2 concepts, which appeared similar to the cranked-kite planform of the U.S. Navy-funded X-47B demonstrator. Around the same time, Northrop also unveiled the Model 437 concept, an autonomous spinoff from the crewed Model 401 Sierra demonstrator. The Model 437 finally emerged as a piloted demonstrator aircraft in 2024. Earlier this year, Northrop announced that the aircraft had transitioned into the Beacon demonstrator, serving as a testbed for mission autonomy technology. body_zh: 诺斯罗普·格鲁曼公司的莲花项目秘密揭晓 hockensmithawi…2025 年 10 月 27 日星期一 - 18:05 一位熟悉该项目的消息人士告诉《航空周刊》，诺斯罗普·格鲁曼公司已在该公司位于加利福尼亚州莫哈韦的规模化复合材料快速原型制造工厂秘密建造了一个大型新型无人驾驶飞机系统 (UAS)，称为“莲花项目”。 《航空周刊》查看的一张飞机照片显示，一架完工的涡轮风扇飞机停在公共机场的 Scaled Composites 园区内。莲花无人机的设计在某些方面类似于新推出的洛克希德·马丁公司 Vectis 项目的特征，其长而细长的机身位于机翼前缘的前面，其机头顶部有后掠边缘，通向细长的尖端。 Lotus 和 Vectis 的设计在许多其他方面存在差异。与 Vectis 飞机的发动机进气口安装在机身中部较低的位置不同，Lotus 进气口位于机身最后部的高处。 Lotus 还拥有急剧倾斜的尾部，与无尾配置的 Vectis 不同。 Lotus 项目似乎代表了诺斯罗普美国空军协同作战飞机 (CCA) Increment 2 计划的候选者，该计划将在明年预定的采购过程之前最终确定竞争性原型机的要求。这张照片显示，诺斯罗普公司已经制造了一架验证机，或许比洛克希德公司的竞争对手设计领先一步，后者预计要到 2027 年才能实现首飞。作为诺斯罗普公司的快速原型制造部门，Scaled Composites 工厂经常秘密制造飞机验证机。今年早些时候，Scaled Composites 向美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 注册了一架涡轮风扇动力固定翼飞机，型号为 444，并授予该组织 N444LX 尾号。目前尚不清楚该注册是否代表 Project Lotus 还是另一个未公开的项目。诺斯罗普还正在为 DARPA 建造 XRQ-73，也称为系列混合电动推进 AiR 演示（Shepard）。在回答《航空周刊》有关莲花项目的问题时，诺斯罗普避免直接回答，但笼统地谈到了其对自动驾驶飞机的内部投资。诺斯罗普表示：“我们的投资优先考虑速度和规模生产，而不牺牲性能或能力。诺斯罗普·格鲁曼团队在生产速度、重量和零件减少以及整体成本效率方面取得了巨大进步。这些进步有利于我们在诺斯罗普·格鲁曼为美国和国际客户生产的一系列自主能力。”正如洛克希德公司的 Vectis 项目设计在 9 月透露的那样，诺斯罗普的 Lotus 项目代表了工业界和空军内部关于 CCA 机队未来方向的长期争论中的一方，争论强调更高的生存能力或更低的成本。 2024 年，空军决定为 CCA Increment 1 计划选定具有竞争力的原型机，在成本和生存能力之间寻求中间立场。通用原子航空系统公司的 YFQ-42 和 Anduril YFQ-44 是大型飞机，采用一些低可观测或隐形技术。但该飞机比 Kratos XQ-58 等飞机更大、更昂贵，并且缺乏 Project Vectis 和 Project Lotus 的隐身功能。 9 月，空军官员表示，他们正在考虑满足 Increment 2 CCA 要求的全方位选择，从出色的生存能力到小型空射系统。 Lotus 项目还为诺斯罗普内部 CCA 概念如何从之前公开发布的想法演变而来提供了新的见解。随着 2023 年空军 CCA 竞争的白热化，诺斯罗普展示了 SG-1 和 SG-2 概念，它们看起来类似于美国海军资助的 X-47B 验证机的曲柄风筝平面图。大约在同一时间，诺斯罗普还推出了 Model 437 概念车，这是载人 Model 401 Sierra 验证机的自主衍生产品。 437 型最终于 2024 年成为有人驾驶验证机。今年早些时候，诺斯罗普宣布该飞机已转变为 Beacon 验证机，作为任务自主技术的测试平台。发行《航空航天日报与国防报告》，2025 年 10 月 28 日 《航空周刊与航天技术》，2025 年 11 月 10 日 文章类型 文章主要类别 飞机与推进系统 作者 Steve Trimble 内容来源 航空航天日报与国防报告 航空周刊与航天技术 从列表中排除？没有标签：UAS、洛克希德·马丁公司、诺斯罗普·格鲁曼公司、协同作战飞机 (CCA) 门控 AWST-MRO ASD 特色图片 snapshot_2025-10-27_scaled_composites_from_gmaps.png 二级类别/子类别 航空航天防御飞机与推进系统 标题中是否有 iframe？关闭 知识中心特色内容 关闭 不呈现广告 关闭 暂时设置为 AWIN 免费增值 关闭
